notes: Both full-paper titles and DOIs verified. Original reference online 2014 / journal 2015. Original p. 10 is PDF page 10, journal p. 134. Original profession main effect is a located candidate, not an established unique match to the broad description; es/p confidence is false for this attribution. Separate original Fisher exact tests on p. 136 concern contradictions (p < .001) and active strategies (p = .001), without printed partial eta-squared for those tests. No statistics converted. Replication p. 332 reports several frequency tests; extracted ATS 33.50 is the explicitly predicted Questionnaire × Information-Type interaction, not a profession comparison. The mixed author verdict concerns broader beliefs-versus-revealing-information findings, not police-versus-community differences. The two extracted statistics must not be treated as matched tests.

original.target_description: Police officers versus matched community members: main effect of profession on frequency of cues in a Profession × Questionnaire (Q1 beliefs vs Q3 revealing information) × Information Type mixed ANOVA. PDF p. 10 (journal p. 134). The description also mentions separate contradictions and active-strategies tests and does not uniquely identify a statistic.

reported_success.quote: we also replicated Masip and Herrero’s (2015) finding of a decrease for behavioral cues, and an increase for contextual information, in Q2 (relative to Q1). However, unlike Masip and Herrero, we found no evidence for the superiority of contextual information over behavioral cues in responding to Q2.
